results.content: President Trump’s approval rating dipped again this week, following a downward trend in support for the president amid the ongoing Iran war and mounting affordability concerns ahead of November’s midterms. The latest survey from The Economist/YouGov, published Monday, found 33 percent of respondents said they approved of how Trump has handled his job as president. Support for the president was split largely along partisan lines, with 79 percent of GOP respondents and only 4 percent of Democratic respondents approving of Trump’s job performance, according to the poll. results.content: President Donald Trump’s approval rating ahead of the midterm elections sits at a lower point than other modern American presidents, according to polling data from the Pew Research Center and Quinnipiac University. Trump’s declining approval rating has driven Democratic hopes that they could retake a majority of seats in both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Trump Approval Rating Compared to Biden, Bush and Obama Quinnipiac University and the Pew Research Center have consistently tracked presidential approval ratings across recent administrations and offer key insights into how Trump’s approval stacks up against his predecessors.
